subfield: Condensed matter / materials physics for energy conversion
motivation: Miyasaka first used organometal halide perovskites as light absorbers in photovoltaic cells (2009). Park then showed that solid-state perovskite cells were stable and efficient (2012). Snaith found that these materials conduct charge as ambipolar semiconductors with long carrier diffusion lengths, which made thin-film planar devices possible (2012–2013). Together their work founded a new class of solution-processable semiconductors, with remarkable defect tolerance, strong absorption and tunable band gaps. In little more than a decade, single-junction cell efficiencies have passed 26%, and perovskite–silicon tandems have gone beyond 33%, surpassing the Shockley–Queisser-limited single-junction silicon. Operando X-ray and neutron studies of ion migration, phase stability and structural dynamics have made these materials a leading topic in solid-state physics. The discovery joins fundamental semiconductor physics to industrial photovoltaics that are now being commercialized, and it has had a major impact on the energy transition.
